- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 1–2%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+3% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 0.5–1.5% per day.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates the drop; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for each negative sentiment day.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias in 30-day horizon: if forecast is >+5% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.3–0.6), model tends to lag true price movements by 1–3 days; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead with slight downward bias.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” values, model often fails to react to market shifts; increase sensitivity by adding 0.1–0.3 to forecast if sentiment turns positive.
